newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ford Australia to produce natural gas car.
newsitem.headline: Ford Australia to produce natural gas car.

text.p: Ford Australia Ltd, a subsidiary of Ford Motor Co, said on Thursday it has become the first Australian car manufacturer to produce a car engineered to run solely on compressed natural gas.

Ford said the limited production run was part of a worldwide effort by the company to explore a range of alternative fuel vehicle options and followed successful field trials with taxi and gas companies in Australia and New Zealand since 1993.
About 25 natural gas vehicle (NGV) Falcon station wagon modes will be built for sale in 1997, Ford said.

Ford Australia's manager for advanced product development, Carolyn Keenan, said natural gas was cheaper, burned more cleanly and was a more plentiful resource in Australia than petrol, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) or diesel.
"And studies indicate that natural gas engines potentially have a lower impact on ozone formation than other fuels," Keenan said in a statement.

She said the trials, involving 10 taxis, showed that fuel costs compared favourably with LPG at about 10 cents per kilometre for natural gas Falcons compared with about six cents per kilometre for LPG equipped vehicles.

Keenan said the natural gas Falcon was different from other NGV car projects in that it was engineered to run only on natural gas and, unlike a dual-fuel conversion, was not compromised by the demands of another fuel.
The car's 4-litre, 6-cylinder engine is optimised to take advantage of the higher energy content of natural gas.
It develops maximum power of 149kW at 4,700 rpm and maximum torque of 339Nm at 2,800 rpm - around 95 percent of its petrol equivalent.
Engine modifications include a much higher compression ratio of 13.5:1 (compared with standard 9.3) via special pistons and a shaved cylinder head with altered combustion chambers.
Injectors for gas replace those for petrol and a uniquely profiled camshaft and reprogrammed EEC-V electronic engine control module completes the under hood changes.
Twin gas tanks under the rear floor replace the petrol tank while a third gas tank is tucked behind the rear seat. With a 210 litre total volume, the car's range is maximised at about 400 km.
